m2_detail: FRED M2 (seasonally adjusted) rose from ~$22,442B in January 2026 to $22,686B in March 2026, a ~$244B expansion over 3 months, confirming an expanding liquidity tide.
calendar_result: April PPI final demand surged +1.4% MoM vs. +0.5% Dow Jones consensus forecast — the largest monthly gain since March 2022 — and +6.0% YoY, signaling deeply hot upstream inflation well above expectations, a clear SHORT signal.
disruption_detail: The US-Iran conflict continues with Strait of Hormuz traffic at a standstill and oil above $100/bbl; the 30-year Treasury yield spiked to a 19-year high of 5.2% on May 19 before easing to ~5.07% by May 22, signaling acute bond market stress; new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh was sworn in May 22 under maximum inflation pressure.
summary: M2 expansion provides a liquidity tailwind, but it is completely overwhelmed by stagflationary headwinds: April PPI printed +1.4% MoM (nearly 3x consensus) and CPI hit 3.8% YoY (above forecast), the Fed is locked hawkish with zero rate cuts priced in for 2026, the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked with oil above $100/bbl, and the 30-year yield nearly breached 5.2% this week. Until there is a confirmed, verifiable Hormuz reopening and at least one cooler-than-expected inflation print, the risk/reward does not support a directional NQ position.
